analysis.title: Weekly Macro and Markets View, 23 November 2026
key_insights: MSCI World fell 8% last week and is in correction territory, down more than 10% from its summer high. Tech led the decline despite no specific bad news.
US semiconductor index fell 17% on the week and Taiwan's equity market had its worst weekly performance since 1990.
Nvidia Q3 revenue rose more than 100% YoY with 75% margins and upbeat guidance, yet the stock fell 37% on the week after founder Jensen Huang's controversial departure and souring AI sentiment.
Anthropic's IPO raised USD 107bn and hit an intraday market cap above USD 2tn, but the initial 40% rally had almost fully faded by Friday.
Zurich believes this is not the end of the cycle and stocks look oversold, though volatility is likely to stay troublesome.
Credit stayed calm. IG widened only 5-10bps while MSCI World fell 8%. HY underperformed, with the CCC vs BB differential at levels last seen in Covid (US) and 2009 (Europe).

Primary credit demand was strong with over USD 50bn of US IG issuance and a USD 32bn chip-backed SpaceX financing. Zurich concludes equity volatility is likely short lived and stocks offer better prospects than credit.

US housing is weak. Building permits fell 7.4% MoM to the lowest since May 2020 and NAHB sentiment is the lowest since 2012. Retail sales ex auto and gas rose 0.5% MoM in October, while industrial production and regional surveys weakened.
Fed minutes show a hawkish bias, making a December rate hike very likely.

UK CPI accelerated to 3.6% YoY in October from 3.5%, core stayed at 2.8%. Retail sales rose 0.7% MoM and unemployment ticked down to 4.6%. The BoE is expected to stay hawkish but market pricing of further tightening looks overdone.
Eurozone core inflation was revised up to 2.6% YoY in October. German PPI is 8.1% YoY while Q3 negotiated wages rose only 2.57% YoY, so wages are not yet amplifying inflation.

Brazil: BRL fell about 5% on the week toward 6 per USD and the BCB intervened. The 10yr yield hit its highest since February 2025 on fiscal worries, limiting scope for easing despite a Q3 GDP contraction (preliminary -0.9% QoQ).
UK and EU agreed a new deal covering food exports, youth mobility and carbon emissions.

market_movers.rationale: Stock fell 37% on the week despite strong Q3 results, on founder Jensen Huang's departure and souring AI sentiment.

sector_views.rationale: Valuations are now cheap but investors fear peaking cyclical earnings. Zurich sees stocks as oversold and does not see the AI cycle ending.
UK stocks outperformed on defensive nature and low tech exposure.
Stocks are seen offering better prospects than credit at the current juncture.

earnings_insights: Nvidia Q3 reported: revenue up more than 100% YoY, margins at 75%, upbeat guidance. The stock still fell 37% on the week.

Unchanged, suggesting underlying pressure is stable.
Down from 4.7%, but October data point to deterioration.
Lowest since May 2020, housing unlikely to improve near term.

macro_indicators.indicator: US retail sales ex auto and gas

macro_indicators.interpretation: Energy cost pass-through still working through, inflation likely to rise further.
Modest wage growth reduces persistence risk but squeezes real incomes.
Weak industry and services, supports Q3 GDP contraction expectation.

risk_factors: Cyclical earnings may be peaking and tech cheapness could be an illusion.
Credit may be underappreciating risk and have significant downside.
Brazil fiscal slippage and BRL weakness.
Persistent eurozone inflation from energy pass-through.
Weak US housing and slowing industrial momentum.
vol_and_positioning: Equity volatility is expected to stay troublesome but likely short lived given calm credit.
CCC vs BB spread differential is at Covid-crisis levels in the US and 2009 levels in Europe.
Primary credit markets show low new issue concessions.
geopolitical: UK and EU agreed a new deal on food exports, youth mobility and carbon emissions.
Brazil fiscal uncertainty after President Lula opposed social spending cuts and delayed naming a finance minister.

tension_points.bull_case: Calm credit and strong primary issuance suggest the AI cycle is intact and equity volatility is short lived.
tension_points.bear_case: Credit may be underappreciating risks and have significant downside, and cyclical earnings may be peaking.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Broader credit spread widening beyond the 5-10bps IG move, or further deterioration in HY such as the CCC vs BB differential.

theme_stances.key_argument: The sell-off is not the end of the cycle and credit stability suggests equity volatility is short lived.
